title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 30
paragraphs: Now if on being taken prisoner he had been brought to King Darius, he would not, I think, have suffered any harm, but Darius would have forgiven him the charge against him. As it was, however, for this very reason—that he might not escape punishment and again become powerful with the king—Artaphrenes the governor of Sardis and Harpagus, who had captured him, when he had reached Sardis on the way to the king, put him to death there and then; and they impaled his body, but embalmed his head and brought it up to Darius at Susa. Darius, on being informed of this, found fault with those who had done it, because they had not brought Histiaeus up to his presence alive; and he bade them wash the head of Histiaeus and give it proper care, and then bury it, as that of one who had been a great benefactor both of the king himself and of the Persians.
